posts.name: Ishan Shishodiya
posts.cooked:
Whenever you register for a course, it’s always a good idea to get familiar with the Grading Policy of it beforehand either through the Grading Document or the dashboard itself. In both places you’d find a mention of BPTs and the OPPE eligibilities.

I can’t comment on how the course introduction was done, but there are a lot of emails sent out regarding assignment announcements and deadlines.

For OPPE practice you can rely on the oppe-practice-* questions in the course VM. The VM has 130+ questions for you to practice. Solving 80-100 of them will easily build your foundations and help you score in the OPPE.

posts.name: Swati Jain
posts.cooked:
To answer all your queries -

Pankaj9988Ji:

I request to authority please give us a course introduction

Course introduction was given even before the registrations began for diploma course selection. We also had instructor’s session after the course began where all these things, the grading policy & BPTs, VM login etc were explained. Whenever you join a course by now you should how to add calendar so that you get notifications.

Also, in the first week of TA sessions as well all the TAs explained about course structure and VM setup.

Pankaj9988Ji:

. I don’t even know about bpt, when I see on my course page bpt1 absent then I realise that I missed it. And after it

Multiple reminders were sent - on discourse, through mail & on course portal notification, even in TA sessions.

Pankaj9988Ji:

And this app font and wokring too is very complicated plz fix it too. Thanks

I think you mean the VM - that’s not complicated it’s a standard way to login across linux servers. Also, in the first week & in multiple sessions we explained how to solve questions there. There is a video on it.

So, I personally feel even when I did this course as well that this course decent communication. Please consider staying updated with the course communication channels.

Thanks & Regards,
Swati Jain

Yes it’s great but can’t u guys make a separate intro Subject course Like posh training where proessor teach what to learn and where to learn.

It make things easier. Students don’t have to see 100things if The professors guide them well. And it’s a big issue for the ones who r alone.

posts.name: Swati Jain
posts.cooked:
You don’t have to see 100 things, even if you don’t attend live sessions, you can do it just follow course page video instructions - there is a video on how to login to vm, and solve assignments on the portal.

POSH is not a course, it’s a training. Plus, don’t understand the use of putting as a separate thing when it’s a part of course curriculum.

Alone - didn’t get you? None of the diploma courses are a group thing.
